---

The module reads an entry's YAML frontmatter with `goccy/go-yaml`, into `map[string]any` for the
snapshot sdd consumes and into typed structs for what the viewer draws. Splitting the frontmatter
from the body below it needs no dependency.

Two properties decide it. The library carries real semver and a maintainer who ships: v1.19.2 dates
from 2026-01-08. The YAML it meets asks little. Across 950 real entry files the graph holds no block
scalar and no multi-line value. It holds scalars, sequences, nested maps, and single-quoted strings
that double a quote to escape it.

Robustness against a malformed file stays a criterion, and the port answers it rather than the
library. A file whose frontmatter will not parse becomes an `application.DocumentIssue` the store
reports, which sdd surfaces through `Snapshot.Health`, so one bad file leaves the rest of a graph
readable. Go returns an error where the Rust question was whether a crate panics.

`gopkg.in/yaml.v3` loses on movement alone. Half the Go ecosystem depends on it and it behaves well.
Its v3.0.1 dates from 2022-05-27, so a defect met in a reader's graph would wait forever.

This retires the choice of `serde_yaml_bw`. That one picked the least bad option in a Rust
ecosystem where `serde_yaml`, `serde_yml` and `serde_yaml_ng` each carry a deprecation or two years
of silence. The whole problem belongs to a stack this project no longer builds on.

Nothing follows from this on its own. It constrains work other entries commission, and the
dependency joins the manifest with the first code that reads a graph file.
